subject: Archaeology
title: The Spread of Farming Across Europe
description: Learn The Spread of Farming Across Europe in one minute.

hook.text: Farming spread across Europe in about 2,500 years. Ancient DNA shows the farmers came too — they did not just share.

buildup.text: Neolithic farmers migrated from Anatolia starting around 7000 BCE, bringing wheat, barley, sheep, and cattle.

discovery.text: DNA from ancient skeletons shows that European hunter-gatherers and incoming farmers were genetically distinct.

twist.text: In some areas, hunter-gatherers vanished entirely. In others, they mixed with farmers. The pattern varied by region.

climax.text: Modern Europeans carry DNA from both groups. The farming revolution was also a migration and a mixing event.

punchline.text: Farming did not just spread across Europe. The farmers themselves walked there.

quiz.question: What did ancient DNA reveal about the spread of farming in Europe?
options: Genetically distinct farmers migrated from Anatolia, bringing agriculture with them
Farming spread through trade without any population movement
